bug_semantics: When phpseclib validates an untrusted X.509 certificate, X509::validateSignature() (caonly=true by default) falls through to testForIntermediate() if the issuer is not already in the CA store. That helper reads the AIA caIssuers uniformResourceIdentifier straight from the certificate and fetchURL() does fsockopen() to the attacker-chosen host and port with no loopback/private/link-local/metadata or port restriction. URL fetching is enabled by default (disable_url_fetch=false; disableURLFetch() is opt-out). The fetched body is used only if it parses as a certificate, so the impact is CWE-918 SSRF / internal recon rather than direct response disclosure.
flaw_origin: The first public write of the AIA chase is f5807e1d4e131ddb4c6de964e6620edb2b457a98 (2018-03-02, 'X509: auto download intermediate certs') by maintainer terrafrost. That single-parent commit added _fetchURL() (unrestricted HTTP fsockopen), _testForIntermediate() (id-ad-caIssuers URI), and wired both into validateSignature() when no trusted issuer is present. The immediate parent 1.0.10 tree mapped the AIA OID but performed no HTTP fetch. The next-day disableURLFetch() helper (ea475743) left fetching on by default. Later 2.0/3.0 ports and the 2025 4.0 X509 split carried the same mechanism; they did not first write it.

reasoning: CVE-2026-55599 / GHSA-m557-wrgg-6rp4 is a published, non-withdrawn SSRF: untrusted AIA caIssuers URLs are fetched during X509 signature validation with fetching on by default and no destination policy. First-party advisory text, the 3.0.53 sink, and git -S/-L all locate the same mechanism. The smallest public first-write is f5807e1d4e131ddb4c6de964e6620edb2b457a98, which introduced _fetchURL/_testForIntermediate and hooked them into validateSignature; the immediate parent 894ac25e (1.0.10) lacks those functions and any X509 HTTP client, so introducer_parent_absent is true after direct parent-tree grep. The commit is a focused single-parent patch, not a merge/squash, so it was not decomposed. Tag checks place the BIC at 1.0.11/2.0.11 (and all 3.0.x), before the patched boundary 1.0.30/2.0.55/3.0.54 landed by 0987dd98 plus 2.0/3.0/4.0 ports. The GHSA >=0.1.1 lower bound overstates pre-2018 versions that had no AIA fetch; that range error does not make the advisory a false positive. AI judgment is BIC-only: the 2018 terrafrost commit object has no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/bot marker, so the verdict is NOT_AI.
